analysis.investment_thesis: Rikhav is a recently-listed micro-cap broker whose 2025 earnings already peaked and rolled over (net profit 42→24 Cr, operating income 55→34 Cr) despite revenue tripling — classic cycle-top margin compression in Indian stockbroking after the SEBI F&O curbs. A 6.6x P/E looks cheap only if you believe trailing earnings are the floor; I suspect they are the ceiling, and the real forward P/E is considerably higher.
key_strengths: Low reported leverage: borrowings collapsed from 40 Cr to 5 Cr; equity up to 244 Cr in 2025
Promoter holds 64.06% — skin in the game, aligned ownership
Headline P/E 6.63 is optically cheap vs. listed broker peers
key_risks: Hyper-cyclical retail broking — earnings already declining post SEBI F&O/derivatives curbs
FY25 OCF of -188 Cr and FCF -189 Cr: only 1 of last 4 years had positive operating cash flow
Micro-cap (159 Cr) with low float/FII-DII ownership (<2%) — liquidity trap if cycle turns
red_flags: Operating margin collapse: OpInc/Revenue fell from ~50% (FY24) to ~10% (FY25)
Net profit down 43% YoY while revenue up 3x — revenue mix shifting to low-margin/pass-through lines
Revenue 9x in 3 years in a broker is the textbook signature of a retail speculation peak
Recently listed (BSE code 544340) — IPO timed to cycle greed
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Second-level thinking here is essential. First-level says: "P/E 6.6, ROE 13%, ROCE 17%, debt-free, promoter owns 64% — bargain." Second-level asks what the price reflects vs. reality. The market is pricing trailing earnings that were generated in the most euphoric retail-trading environment India has seen in a generation. FY25 already shows the cycle turning: revenue tripled to 328 Cr but net profit fell from 42 to 24 Cr and operating income nearly halved from 55 to 34 Cr. That is textbook margin compression as retail F&O volumes normalize post the Oct-2024 SEBI lot-size/expiry rules. The 6.6x multiple on peak-cycle-minus-one earnings is not a margin of safety — it is a mirage.

The cash flow statement is the tell. Operating cash flow was -188 Cr in FY25 on 24 Cr of reported profit; only 1 of the last 4 years produced positive OCF. Brokers have working-capital swings (client funds, exchange margins), but that gap is large enough to demand scrutiny. Combine this with a 159 Cr micro-cap, tiny institutional ownership (<2% combined FII+DII), and a listing that appears to have been timed to the cycle peak, and the asymmetry is wrong-way: limited upside if things stay good, 50-70% drawdown risk if Nifty and retail volumes correct together. I would want this at 3-4x normalized earnings, not 6.6x peak earnings. Pass.
